messages:
Priya (support): Hey team, customer Sam (Acme Corp) opened an escalation — p95/p99 for text-generation API jumped from ~350ms to 1.9s starting ~09:10 UTC. They're hitting production and it's impacting their UI. They pasted a couple request ids: req-8a3f2, req-8a3f9. Sam says this started right after a spike of long-context requests (>=16k tokens).

Sam (customer): yes, saw lots of slow responses and a bunch of 504s. We didn't change client side. Here's an example curl reproducer we used:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-llm-xl","input":"<16k tokens of docs>"}'
```

Priya (support): thanks. I've collected the two request ids and forwarded to eng. Noticed spikes in queuing_time in the dashboards. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/d/queues/worker-overview (internal) :eyes:

Alex (eng-sre): pulling logs for req-8a3f2 / req-8a3f9 now. Early guess: long-sequence requests are blowing up batch sizes and causing head-of-line blocking in the serving pool. Can someone post recent autoscaler/worker counts?

observability-bot: metric snapshot 09:12-09:20 UTC for service=runtime-worker: p50=220ms, p95=1.85s, p99=3.2s, mean_queue_length=18, max_inflight=128, batch_size_avg=42 (normal: ~8-12).

Lee (eng-runtime): confirmed. We see continuous batching mode ended up grouping many long requests — average batch size jumped which increases per-token latency. Also admission-control queue length shot up. Snippet from worker logs: 

```
[2026-03-15T09:13:02Z] WARN admission: queue_time_ms=1620 inflight=120 queued=34 max_concurrency=128
[2026-03-15T09:13:05Z] INFO batch_exec: batch_size=76 seq_len_max=16384 exec_time_ms=2780
[2026-03-15T09:13:05Z] ERROR serve: request req-8a3f2 timeout after 2500ms
```

Alex (eng-sre): that `batch_size=76` and `seq_len_max=16384` is killer — throughput suffers superlinearly. Two angles: a) admission control should cap batch_size by effective token budget, b) fallback routing to a cheaper (lower-latency) model variant for extremely-long sequences. For immediate mitigation I can drop max_batch_size and enforce per-request token budget.

Priya (support): customer says any temporary tweak is fine as long as their UI recovers. They prefer faster responses even if quality drops slightly.

Lee (eng-runtime): proposed emergency steps (I can run these now):
1) Reduce worker MAX_BATCH_SIZE from 128 -> 16 (config flip via /admin/config/admission).
2) Set admission controller to reject requests with seq_len > 12k with a clear 413 response (client can retry truncated).
3) Enable `fast-variant` routing: route requests with seq_len>8k to model=open-llm-medium (lower latency).
4) Temporarily scale up worker pool by +30% (kubectl scale deployment/runtime-worker --replicas=65 -> 85).

Alex (eng-sre): +1. Also, to avoid thrashing maybe cap max_inflight to 96 while batch_size is lowered. I'll push the `max_inflight` flag to 96 in the admission config.

deploy-bot: submitted rollout change admission-config v2026-03-15-09-22 by lee -> started

Lee (eng-runtime): applied changes:
```
POST https://admin.redwood/internal/config/admission 
payload: {"MAX_BATCH_SIZE":16, "MAX_INFLIGHT":96, "SEQ_LEN_REJECT_THRESHOLD":12000, "FALLBACK_MODEL_FOR_LONG_SEQ":"open-llm-medium"}
```

observability-bot: post-change metrics (09:27-09:34 UTC): p50=210ms, p95=420ms, p99=920ms, mean_queue_length=6, batch_size_avg=12, max_inflight=96. Error 504 rate dropped from 4.5% -> 0.6%

Priya (support): Customer reports UI latency recovered and 504s mostly gone. They accepted the short-term model fallback. Sam: can you confirm?

Sam (customer): Confirmed. Back to acceptable. We saw one truncated response when seq_len hit 13k (expected). Thanks for the fast turnaround.

Alex (eng-sre): root cause summary for postmortem draft: sudden traffic of many extreme-long-context requests increased effective batch token budget, which skyrocketed batch sizes and per-batch execution time. Admission controller had permissive batch/inflight limits and autoscaler reacted too slowly (scale lag + metrics emitter sampling every 60s). This caused queueing/backpressure and head-of-line blocking leading to p95/p99 regressions.

Priya (support): created ticket SUP-4021 linking customer support logs, request ids, and mitigation timeline.

Lee (eng-runtime): follow-ups I will do in the next 24h:
- implement token-budget-aware batching (cap batch by sum(seq_len) not count)
- reduce autoscaler scrape interval to 10s for critical metrics
- add a circuit that proactively routes long seqs to fallback models instead of queuing them
- add a richer telemetry tag for model_variant + seq_len in logs so support can filter fast.

Alex (eng-sre): I'll add a guard in admission controller to avoid batch_size growth beyond token budget and add an emergency runbook: `runbook/queueing-backpressure.md` with quick commands used today (kubectl scale, config flip endpoints, dashboards to check).

Priya (support): closing thread — customer happy for now. Will keep open for the postmortem. :thumbsup:
